The option "Maximum time before CTA is sent" sets the maximum amount of time in hours before a Call-To-Action (CTA) link is sent after the last client or your reply. If this value is greater than 0, the system will 'close' each conversation after this specified time. This ensures that a CTA link is sent even if the user does not respond within that time frame.

For example, if the "Maximum time before CTA is sent" is set to 0 hours, the CTA link will be sent immediately after the last reply without any delay. If it is set to 4 hours, the system will wait for 4 hours after the last reply before sending the CTA link, regardless of whether there was further interaction in the conversation.

Instagram definition:
- Tap at the bottom to go to Search & Explore.
- Tap Search in the search bar at the top.
- Type who or what you want to search for, then tap the search button in the bottom right of your keyboard.

If you missed this... This is how new Reactions Pro module algorithms works:

- 1:1 - like and view story only together, at a time
- 1:1 + M - like and view story only together like in 1:1 + you will be able to continue doing masslooking (mass story view) when story like limit will be reached
- Basic - mark stories as seen vary on batch size (we can mark as seen N stories per request, by default it's 10), after that do a story like (we can do only 1 per API request), actions works separately, that's mean if story like will be limited, you will be able to continue to do massloooking, and if massloooking will be limited, you will be able to continue to do story likes.
- Advanced - the same as Basic, but with activity pause between story likes actions, in Basic we simply skip story like action if delay is not passed (will help perfom other mass actions faster)

In conclusion: I think 1:1 and 1:1 + M better for now. And 1:1 + M is best choice for users who want to use masslooking (mass story view) without story likes also. The negative part of Basic and Advanced algorithms is possible timings resynchronization that can cause situations when you will mark as seen and like different stories (not the same stories) like in 1+1 or 1+1 + M algorithms.
